oracle_policy: All literal expected states/receipts/requests/outputs/stores/failures are independently constructed from typed definitions and action tables; no candidate runner constructs its expected output. Exact API field names and concrete grant/template constructors must be refreshed against accepted M2/M3 before official freeze.
fixture_universe: Finite two domains/two assets and distinct source/recipient/administrator principals; full nonempty capability store contains explicit allocated IDs, nextId and active/inactive cases. Where a fixture overrides this universe, the override is explicit.

fixtures.name: Empty participant universe
fixtures.inputs: B empty, empty roster/tree/schedule; world contains a USD sentinel11 and nonempty capability store with explicit nextId/revocation data.
fixtures.expected: Admission succeeds; full world/store unchanged, no locals/attempts. Nonempty B with empty tree is structurally rejected after successful base checks.

fixtures.name: Stable identities and empty nodes
fixtures.inputs: B ordered[b0,b1,b2], all branches empty; compare fork(fork(b0,b1),b2), fork(b0,fork(b1,b2)), and empty-node wrappers with empty schedule.
fixtures.expected: Each identity occurs once; same full empty-local observation and full entry world. Reordered leaves also preserve identities for a fixed named schedule in F05.

fixtures.name: Duplicate and missing identities
fixtures.inputs: Tree leaves[b0,b0,b2], then leaves[b0,b2], valid configuration and complete base schedule.
fixtures.expected: First mismatch in roster order is b0 expected1 observed2, then b1 expected1 observed0. Neither creates a machine or attempt; entry world/store retained.

fixtures.name: Deterministic base precedence
fixtures.inputs: Combine malformed tree with invalid catalog; then valid catalog plus malformed full branch suffix; then structurally valid branches with count mismatch.
fixtures.expected: Actual base configuration, then roster-first structural LocalFailure, then roster-first schedule mismatch wins before tree error. A financially unreachable malformed suffix remains checked.

fixtures.name: Disjoint three streams all90 schedules
fixtures.inputs: Common finite universe: home/away, USD/EUR, source principals v0/v1/v2, recipients r0/r1/r2 and sentinel. Initial home/USD(v0,v1,v2)=(7,5,4), recipients0; away/EUR sentinel11, other cells0. Full nonempty store has literal valid grants. Branch i uses distinct component ci, producer operation100+100*i and consumer101+100*i. The zero-effect producer at index0 exports its own vi balance under qualified(ci,budget); index1 transfers that own-history amount vi→ri and exports no outputs. Boundaries authenticate vi at each own position; literal grant IDs1–6 authorize the corresponding source/target/domain/asset operations.
fixtures.expected: All90 schedules with multiplicities(2,2,2) succeed. Final sources(0,0,0), recipients(7,5,4), sentinel11, store exact. Every local consumed2/nextIndex2 with literal producer/consumer receipts and histories containing exactly the producer snapshot7/5/4 respectively (consumer exports none). For each schedule construct full raw event/attempt worlds chronologically from the independent action table; compare multiple groupings and isolated reference.

fixtures.name: Compatible financial refusal all90 schedules
fixtures.inputs: F05 except b1 consumer requests literal6 from v1=5; no custom financial guard masks the actual typed insufficient-funds check.
fixtures.expected: All90 schedules retain v1=5,r1=0; b0/b2 transfer7/4. b1 consumed2,nextIndex1, exact located .kernel .insufficientFunds at index1, producer history retained. Final canonical observations agree although raw worlds/attempt order differ.

fixtures.name: Peer continuation and failed suffix
fixtures.inputs: F06 raw prefix schedule[b1,b1,b1,b0,b0,b2,b2,b1], deliberately over-complete.
fixtures.expected: b1 consumed4,nextIndex1 and first index1 refusal retained; two skipped tokens append no attempts. Peers complete, six actual attempts total, final balances as F06. No ancestor cancellation.

fixtures.name: Absolute boundary and branch selection
fixtures.inputs: Funded two-step branch with index0 producer and index1 consumer; boundary principal authorized only at its own correct index, with distinct now/environment witnesses. Include an unselected peer with a different principal.
fixtures.expected: Correct second leaf uses own nextIndex1 and own history; constant boundary0 changes authority or receipt. Branch selection is by consumed; arbitrary-entry companion distinguishes consumed from nextIndex without asserting reachability.

fixtures.name: Tree path re-encoding and errors
fixtures.inputs: Encode stable schedule[b0,b1,b0,b2,b1,b2] for both three-leaf groupings; add paths ending at a fork/empty, beyond a leaf, and an invalid suffix after two valid paths.
fixtures.expected: Decoded names match exactly after re-encoding, not after copying paths. First invalid path reports its full path and token index2 in appended suffix case, before financial/admission work.

fixtures.name: Raw malformed fallback
fixtures.inputs: Use a raw duplicate local tree with distinct populated b0 locals and a missing b1; bypass admitted runner explicitly.
fixtures.expected: b0 selects only the first depth-first match; absent b1 leaves full machine unchanged. Admitted runner still rejects this shape. This does not instantiate well-formed-tree simulation.

fixtures.name: Populated entry continuation
fixtures.inputs: Construct related populated trees/flat machine with p0 producer history/index1/consumed1, p1 already failed and consumed1, nonempty exact attempts/store, and p2 untouched. Continue same suffix and compare two chunks/three tree shapes.
fixtures.expected: No history, world, failure, index or store reset. Exact full representation equality holds on arbitrary related entries; separate reachable construction is supplied where claimed.

fixtures.name: Shared qualified key own-history separation
fixtures.inputs: Shared cell q7: b0 first reads/exports q7; b1 first transfers2 q→sink and exports q5 under the same qualified key; then b0 transfers its stored7 from v0=7, b1 its stored5 from v1=5. Schedule[b0,b1,b0,b1], b2 empty.
fixtures.expected: Final q5,sink2,v0=v1=0,r0=7,r1=5. Separate stream snapshots remain7/5. Both tree shapes agree fully for this fixed schedule; disjoint admission rejects shared read/write footprints. No cross-stream history support is added.

fixtures.name: All compatibility directions
fixtures.inputs: Use separate valid fixtures for write/write conflict, i-write/j-read-only conflict and j-write/i-read-only conflict, plus allowed shared read-only overlap; include output-only read dependency.
fixtures.expected: Canonical roster pair, existing ConflictKind and first offending exact cell are reported. Read-only sharing succeeds. Output-snapshot dependencies participate in analyzed compatibility.

fixtures.name: Overlapping fixed-schedule equality
fixtures.inputs: Two authorized withdrawals7/6 from shared home/USD vault10 into distinct recipients; b2 empty. Fix[b0,b1], through both the stable-name runner and its correctly encoded path wrapper.
fixtures.expected: Every valid grouping yields vault3,recipient0=7,recipient1=0 and b1 exact insufficientFunds refusal; compatibility fails but ordinary shared admission/execution succeeds.

fixtures.name: Schedule-independence counterexample
fixtures.inputs: F14 compare[b0,b1] with[b1,b0].
fixtures.expected: Vault3 versus4; distinct recipient and refusal identity. Both schedules complete and valid; pairwise compatibility premise is false. This refutes unrestricted schedule independence only.

fixtures.name: Global edge omission is material
fixtures.inputs: Global binding edges A=B and B=C with initialized balances5/5/5. Only C transfers1 to sink0 in a valid authorized branch; compare tree cuts retaining only A=B versus the actual full set.
fixtures.expected: Actual result A5/B5/C4/sink1: full binding query false, truncated A=B query true. Compatibility/admission does not supply binding preservation; the needed local obligation fails.

fixtures.name: Initialized M2 contract transport
fixtures.inputs: Three streams each perform an authorized paired debit1 from A and B to sink, start5/5/0, same global A=B edge and total region A+B+sink=10. Use actual accepted M2 semantics after dependency refresh.
fixtures.expected: Each prefix gives(4,4,2),(3,3,4),(2,2,6) in token-count order; all groupings preserve initialized equality and total through M3 local/cross obligations. Overlap precludes disjoint-theorem use. Initial4/5/0 companion remains unequal.

fixtures.name: Causal monitor transport and order limit
fixtures.inputs: Use accepted M3 funded producer6/consumer6 plus peer deposits1/2, initial vault10/donors2,3/recipient0. Fixed update and initial monitor are identical across trees. Add a monitor recording selected identities and a skipped-token companion.
fixtures.expected: For each of12 complete schedules, fixed-schedule trees match full base/monitor states and actual appended-attempt inputs; reserve≥4 and final vault7. Order-list monitors differ across distinct schedules, even for disjoint identity actions.

fixtures.name: Full versus canonical synthetic observations
fixtures.inputs: Arbitrary labeled machine pairs differ in exactly one field: world cell, store/nextId/revocation, consumed, nextIndex, failure/index, output, event receipt/request, raw event world, global attempt/outcome.
fixtures.expected: Full comparison rejects every listed difference. Canonical comparison rejects all retained-field differences but accepts differences only in raw intermediate worlds/global attempt order. No pair is labeled reachable or a financial execution merely because constructible.

fixtures.name: Merge retains base and unique owner
fixtures.inputs: Run disjoint empty/identity/transfer leaves from same base with nonzero unowned sentinel11 and distinct owner balances. Include empty subtree at each side and a refused owner retaining a successful prefix.
fixtures.expected: Merge chooses each owner final balance exactly once and initial sentinel11; never doubles to22. Full capabilities unchanged; empty subtree units and outside-write frame hold.
